Recenpt APA study on violence in video games has several shortcomings, only points out that there is insufficient data on the subject.
THERE IS INSUFFICIENT DATA FOR A MEANINGFUL ANSWER

Within the last few paragraphs of this study, the task force recommends the ESRB to change their rating systems to be more empirical and explain just what type of violence is shown in the game. This is ridiculous because there is no way a person can calculate how “violent” an act is, there is no equations proving that the amount of “violence” generated by 3 stabbings are equal one shooting, it is all subjective.

This stood out for me. It's another "how much of this author's commentary can be trusted?" flags. First they describe the task force's recommendation that the ESRB change their rating to explain just what type of violence is in the game.

Then he goes on to complain that you can't quantify violence. Nobody was asking the ESRB to calculate how violent something is. They're asking for the ESRB to describe in more detail the nature of the violence. I don't think it's particularly difficult to tell the difference between asking the ESRB to change "violence" to "graphic war violence" or "bloody criminal violence" and getting them to list a rating for how severe the violence is. They're two completely different things.

The author is right in that they task force wasn't able to draw any conclusions from the review, and the fact that they concluded that they couldn't draw any conclusions is indicative of objectivity. It's a good thing. Some researchers feel that they need to arrive at a conclusion whether the findings support one or not. It would be nice if the author had mentioned that as part of the review, but it's clear they had some other blockages of their own to deal with.
